ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows rectangle ABCD with A at the upper left, B at the upper right, C at the lower right, and D at the lower left. A diagonal from D to B is drawn and labeled 56 ft. Reasoning: The problem states that each diagonal of rectangle ABCD is 56 feet, so diagonal AC is also 56 feet. In right triangle ABC, angle B is 90 degrees, AC is the hypotenuse, and angle BAC is 42 degrees. Side AB is adjacent to angle BAC, so cos(42°) = AB / AC. method.method_draft: Use the midpoint/intersection property of rectangle diagonals. Let O be the intersection of diagonals AC and BD. Since rectangle diagonals are congruent and bisect each other, OA = OB = 28 ft. Because O lies on AC, ∠BAO = ∠BAC = 42°. Triangle AOB is isosceles with OA = OB, so ∠ABO = 42° and ∠AOB = 180° − 42° − 42° = 96°. Apply the Law of Cosines in triangle AOB: AB² = 28² + 28² − 2(28)(28)cos(96°). Then take the square root and round to get AB ≈ 41.6 ft.
